newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria buys 70,000 tonnes of sugar this month.
newsitem.headline: Algeria buys 70,000 tonnes of sugar this month.

text.p: Algeria, suffering from a shortage of sugar for its domestic market in the past few weeks, has bought 70,000 tonnes of sugar, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Sunday.

Algeria's state-owned companies, Entreprise Nationale de Sucre (ENASUCRE) and Entreprise Nationale pour l'Approvisionnement en Produits Alimentaires (ENAPAL), and some private importers had concluded contracts with unspecified foreign suppliers for the 70,000 tonnes, said APS, quoting Algerian officials.
Lack of hard currency funds had prevented ENASUCRE and ENAPAL from reaching such deals earlier, domestic market director at the Algerian trade ministry, Ammar Boularak, said on Sunday.

"Being out of stock in sugar was due mainly to lack of necessary funds to allow ENAPAL and ENASUCRE to conclude buying deals in the international market," said Ammar quoted by the Algerian state-run radio.
